:::{#thm-lotus}
#### Law of the Unconscious Statistician (LOTUS)

**Discrete case.**
For any function $g$ of a *discrete* random variable $X$
[@wikipedia_law_of_the_unconscious_statistician]:

$$\E{g(X)} = \sum_{x \in \rangef{X}} g(x) \cd \P(X=x)$$

**Continuous case.**
For any function $g$ of a *continuous* random variable $X$ with density $\p(X=x)$:

$$\E{g(X)} = \int_{x \in \rangef{X}} g(x) \cd \p(X=x)\, dx$$

:::

::: proof

We prove the discrete case.
Let $Y = g(X)$.
For each $y \in \rangef{Y}$, the event $\{Y = y\}$ is the disjoint union
of the events $\{X = x\}$ over the values $x$ with $g(x) = y$,
and each $x \in \rangef{X}$ belongs to exactly one such group.

$$
\ba
\E{g(X)}
&= \E{Y} && \text{(substitution } Y = g(X) \text{)}
\\&= \sum_{y \in \rangef{Y}} y \cd \P(Y=y) && \text{(definition of expectation for discrete r.v.)}
\\&= \sum_{y \in \rangef{Y}} y \cd \sum_{\substack{x \in \rangef{X} \\ g(x) = y}} \P(X=x) && \text{(countable additivity over the disjoint events } \{X = x\} \text{)}
\\&= \sum_{y \in \rangef{Y}} \sum_{\substack{x \in \rangef{X} \\ g(x) = y}} y \cd \P(X=x) && \text{(distribute } y \text{ into the inner sum)}
\\&= \sum_{y \in \rangef{Y}} \sum_{\substack{x \in \rangef{X} \\ g(x) = y}} g(x) \cd \P(X=x) && \text{(} y = g(x) \text{ for every term of the inner sum)}
\\&= \sum_{x \in \rangef{X}} g(x) \cd \P(X=x) && \text{(the groups partition } \rangef{X} \text{)}
\ea
$$

The last step regroups a possibly infinite sum,
which is valid because $\E{g(X)}$ is defined only when the sum converges absolutely.

:::

::: {.remark .notes}

LOTUS says that to compute $\E{g(X)}$,
we do not need to first find the distribution of $g(X)$;
we can compute the expectation directly using the distribution of $X$.
The continuous case is the density-weighted analogue of this argument,
but a fully rigorous proof needs the general change-of-variables
theorem for integrals against a pushforward measure --- approximating
$g$ by simple functions and passing to the limit --- which is beyond
this page's scope
[@billingsley1995probability; @gut2013; @CaseBerg01; @wp:lotus].

:::
